title: Sample 14-10: Conclusion of Play

illustrates.quote: A phrase indicating the conclusion of the play (e.g., “The End” or “The Curtain Falls,” etc.) is centered and preceded and followed by a blank line.

blocks.speaker: Webster
blocks.text: **Webster** (*moving to center stage, and joining* Jabez' *hands and* Mary’s). And whom God hath joined let no man put asunder. (*He kisses* Mary *and turns, dusting his hands.*) Well, that job’s done. I hope there’s pie for breakfast, neighbor Stone.
(*And, as some of the women, dancing, bring in pies from the kitchen*)

resolution: A/B agreed on braille (byte-for-byte) and on print substance; both described the bold/italic emphasis only in prose `features` fields (B) or left it out of `text` (A) rather than marking it in place. Per this repo's own established convention, `text` was rewritten with **Webster**/*Jabez'*/*Mary's).*'/*Mary* embedded directly — the exact italic-run boundary (including the closing paren and period right after ‘Mary’s’) was determined by forward-translation testing until an EXACT MATCH was reached, matching Example 14-4's own already-documented italic-terminator behaviour. A's own illustrates.rule/quote (14.8.1, the actual rule text) kept over B's own null/title-repeat. Forward-translated through Emboss's translator (one {type:'play',subtype:'prose'} block with bold/italic segments, one {type:'stage'} block, one centred {type:'heading'} block): EXACT MATCH (see differences.md). Print description corrected 23 Sep 2026 (see printCorrections).
